subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the volume of the tetrahedron having the edges i+j+k, i−j and i+2j+k.

mark_split.label: Divide by 6 and state the volume

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.64 — SAQ chapter 9 Product of Vectors, answer 60. Printed appearances: AP 16. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. recall_prompt: Say how you would find the volume of a tetrahedron from its three edges.

steps.label: State the formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. The three given vectors are already the EDGES from one corner, so they go straight into the formula with no subtraction needed.
steps.memory_tip: The three given vectors are already EDGES from one corner, so no subtraction is needed.
lines: Let a = i + j + k, b = i − j, c = i + 2j + k
Volume of the tetrahedron with edges a, b, c is

recall.must_convey: That the volume of a tetrahedron on three edge vectors is one sixth of the modulus of their scalar triple product.
accept: the volume is one sixth of the modulus of the scalar triple product
write the formula, one by six times mod of a b c box product
volume equals one sixth the triple product
volume formula one by six into mod of a b c

steps.why: The scalar triple product is the volume of the parallelepiped on the three edges; a tetrahedron is one sixth of that box.
common_mistakes: Using ½ instead of ⅙, which is the triangle factor, not the tetrahedron one.
Omitting the modulus and reporting a negative volume.

steps.label: Evaluate the triple product
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. The scalar triple product is a 3×3 determinant with the three edges as rows. Note b has a zero k component — write it in.
steps.memory_tip: A 3×3 determinant with the three edges as rows. b has a zero k component — write it in.

recall.must_convey: That the scalar triple product is a determinant with the three edges as rows, evaluating to 1.
accept: put the three edges as rows of a determinant and expand to get one
the triple product determinant comes to one
evaluate the three by three determinant, the answer is one
moodu edges ni rows ga petti determinant expand cheste one vasthundi

steps.why: A zero component still occupies its column. Leaving it out would shift the whole row and change the determinant.
common_mistakes: Missing the zero k component of b.
Getting the plus-minus-plus sign pattern wrong.

steps.label: Divide by 6
steps.margin_note: Last mark. One sixth of 1. A volume is reported in cubic units — say so.
steps.memory_tip: One sixth of the triple product, reported in CUBIC units.

recall.must_convey: That the volume is one sixth of 1, that is 1/6 cubic units.
accept: one sixth of one is one sixth cubic units
the volume is one by six cubic units
divide by six to get one sixth
one by six cubic units vasthundi
the answer is one sixth of a cubic unit

steps.why: The modulus matters even when the number is positive: a determinant can come out negative, and a volume never can.
common_mistakes: Writing square units instead of cubic.

insider_note: A tetrahedron is one SIXTH of the box product, not one half. The determinant comes to 1, so the whole answer is 1/6 — a small number is correct here.
